skill.name: security-report
skill.description: Generate DOCX security assessment reports with findings, risk ratings, remediation guidance, and executive-ready structure.
skill.summary: Creates structured DOCX security assessment reports with risk ratings and remediation plans.
skill.author: BytR-Ecosystems

content.value_statement: Security teams need consistent reports that explain risk, evidence, and remediation clearly. This skill guides DOCX report creation with standard sections, severity colors, findings tables, and remediation timelines.
actual_capabilities: Defines a DOCX security assessment report structure.
Provides Python guidance for python-docx report generation.
Specifies risk rating colors for common severity levels.
Organizes findings by severity with evidence and remediation fields.
Includes guidance for remediation timelines and executive summaries.
limitations: Does not perform vulnerability scanning or exploit validation.
Does not include ready-made DOCX templates or scripts.
Requires user-provided findings, evidence, and scope details.
Referenced advanced materials may need separate review when available.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Audit Reports
use_cases.description: Create a consistent DOCX report after a security assessment or penetration test.

use_cases.title: Summarize Internal Risk
use_cases.description: Turn validated findings into an executive-ready report with severity ordering and remediation plans.

use_cases.title: Document Compliance Gaps
use_cases.description: Organize compliance observations into structured findings with evidence, impact, and recommended fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner report generation from a short finding list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DOCX security assessment report using these findings, scope, and client details. Include severity, evidence, and remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Executive Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a one-page executive summary for this assessment. Explain business impact, top risks, and recommended next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Findings by Severity
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these vulnerability notes into detailed findings. Sort them by severity and include CVSS, evidence, remediation, and references.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Remediation Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a remediation roadmap for these findings. Group fixes by priority, owner, dependency, and expected completion timeline.

output_examples.input: A penetration test found weak TLS settings, exposed admin panels, and missing multi-factor authentication.
output: Executive summary with the highest business risks first.
Severity-sorted findings with evidence and remediation guidance.
Roadmap that prioritizes MFA and administrative exposure fixes.

output_examples.input: A compliance review identified password policy gaps and incomplete audit logging.
output: Compliance gap report with scope and methodology sections.
Finding table that separates policy, evidence, impact, and corrective action.
Remediation timeline for policy updates and logging improvements.

best_practices: Provide validated findings, affected assets, evidence, and business context before generating the report.
Keep executive summaries short and focused on risk, impact, and decisions.
Review every remediation recommendation with technical owners before distribution.
anti_patterns: Do not present unverified scanner output as confirmed findings.
Do not omit scope, methodology, or evidence from the final report.
Do not use severity colors without clear rating definitions.

faq.question: Does this skill scan systems for vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It helps create reports from findings and evidence that you provide.

faq.question: What file format does it target?
faq.answer: It targets DOCX reports created with python-docx guidance.

faq.question: Can it calculate CVSS scores?
faq.answer: It can include CVSS fields, but scoring should be reviewed against an approved methodology.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Security consultants, internal security teams, and compliance teams can use it for structured reporting.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide scope, methodology, findings, evidence, asset details, severity ratings, and remediation requirements.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
